findings.title: orders query became slower
findings.detail: Mean execution time increased from 8 ms to 26 ms against the stored baseline.
caveats: The finding describes database-side query latency, not upstream request latency.

findings.title: connection usage is high
findings.detail: 87 percent of configured connection slots are currently in use.

impact.basis: current connection slots versus configured maximum

findings.title: orders relies heavily on sequential scans
findings.detail: Sequential scan activity is materially high for the orders relation.
evidence: seq scans materially exceed the expected indexed-access pattern
caveats: Sequential scans can be correct for small tables or queries that read most rows.

findings.title: transaction lock contention dominates sampled waits
findings.detail: A sustained named transaction blocker is present in the sampled wait profile.

findings.title: transaction ID age is close to wraparound
findings.detail: The oldest transaction ID age is 1.8 billion, close to PostgreSQL's wraparound safety wall.

findings.title: legacy index has not been used
findings.detail: This finding is intentionally suppressed in the source policy.
